title: Adding scenarios to courses
intro: Semester → Courses → Scenarios. Research into selecting reusable scenarios from institutional and personal libraries, placing them in a course, and managing their sequence and course-specific settings. Scenario authoring is out of scope; events, competencies, learner visibility and Canvas hand-off are neighbouring concerns.

questions.title: Library browse UX: search, filters (tags, competency, duration), preview before adding
questions.answer: Figma separates finding a reusable item from inspecting and inserting it: Assets search and library filters lead to a Details preview with provenance and “Insert instance” (refero:flow-5039; refero:screen-2e0d5f12). Canva keeps a large preview visible while options change (refero:flow-8062). MasterClass supplies compact category/filter discovery, but in a learner context (mobbin:666b7eaa-84c1-4d32-a152-9b6ae3ae9eb9). For Essentials, combine searchable institutional/own libraries with optional scenario inspection and a persistent selection basket. Competency, duration and equipment filters are proposed domain adaptations, not demonstrated together by this set.

questions.title: Multi-select and batch add vs. one at a time
questions.answer: Teachable imports checked lessons from a source course into a destination curriculum (mobbin:e8676237-6e24-4e98-90a2-e37bfa82f60a). PandaDoc makes batch scope explicit with “Add 2 items” and confirms insertion in the document (mobbin:7833133c-7d81-4179-86a5-6ba8ce80b92c). Canva offers a single-design “Copy to course” / “Move” choice (mobbin:4fb0fdd5-431c-4702-9bb5-fbcb4d78c2df). Circle’s one-question authoring flow is a counterexample for this reuse task (mobbin:327fbad0-5e87-48c9-b7cf-fb0f5bcce035). Essentials should let instructors select several known scenarios, review a count, and add them once into a chosen section.

questions.title: Instance vs. reference semantics (edits to master propagate? per-course overrides?)
questions.answer: Figma visibly inserts a library instance, identifies its source and offers a variable-mode choice (refero:flow-5040). Ditto explicitly attaches selected text to a named library component and confirms the relationship (mobbin:9d28e0e2-ba12-4eb5-9a77-c3227f36b647). Notion exposes “Synced block,” while Canva shows a choose-and-edit handoff; neither capture establishes later synchronization (mobbin:b8778e0e-13d3-49a6-9f01-3680ea66249b; refero:flow-8062-q3). None of these captures verifies master-update propagation or override survival. Essentials needs an explicit decision on linked version, pinned copy and course-only settings before choosing interaction copy.

questions.title: Sequencing after add (drag reorder, grouping into sections, prerequisites between items)
questions.answer: Circle supplies direct before/after evidence of moving a whole section while preserving its lessons and Draft labels (mobbin:0489e85e-877c-41fc-92dc-6e6e7bc9c7da). Kajabi makes grouped content and Draft/Publish/Drip/Lock states visible; Podia shows a delayed section; Teachable exposes date- or enrollment-based section release (mobbin:5b4497cf-d3c9-445f-bff6-754fbbb1cf7c; mobbin:0aed2e1a-0de0-4f32-9dba-2d5a627a1e87; mobbin:e84f7cdf-c9b2-4a3d-bddf-31e53e19e509). The evidence supports in-place grouping and sequence management. It does not demonstrate item-prerequisite configuration. Keep sequence distinct from event scheduling and learner release.

questions.title: Metadata carried along (competencies, duration, equipment) and shown in the outline
questions.answer: Mindvalley, MasterClass and Udemy retain activity titles, numbering and duration in learner outlines (mobbin:99d3f73c-a804-4e4d-9b11-132afbe8ab1c; mobbin:eeaba88c-51dc-44b0-8c15-cf8775b9c361; mobbin:987d1aea-1d31-4f63-ae58-5989ee6837c7). These support a scannable outline, but they do not show metadata being copied by an instructor from a master library. For Essentials, duration, competencies and equipment are candidate course-row fields; their provenance, editability and learner visibility remain design decisions. Event links should lead to the Events sub-module rather than imply that adding a scenario schedules it.

questions.title: Empty / first-run state and suggestions
questions.answer: Podia reduces first-run uncertainty with lightweight guidance and example content; Kajabi shows an editable starter outline (mobbin:6d57146d-b827-45d3-800f-d925dc03c06c; mobbin:8edcefcc-f539-46e6-a13a-d0ed44fa3308). Teachable offers outline methods and an explained empty course list (refero:screen-4f0eb823; refero:flow-9573-q6). Circle shows an empty section with inline add controls but no library route in the captured state (mobbin:5341f9e1-8516-4a2f-b941-a3ef17a2f63f). Essentials should open with “Browse scenario library,” optional suggested scenarios and clear empty/search-empty states. MasterClass’s captured no-results message coexists with an unrelated course card, making the search state ambiguous (refero:screen-75721406). Suggested items should remain editable and should not silently become scheduled learner activities.

references.title: Template preview with live customization
references.question: Q1
references.take: Suggested templates remain visible beside a live customizable preview and Use Canva Editor, but search/filter and course-add are absent.

references.title: Asset library selection and filtering
references.question: Q1
references.take: Figma exposes an Assets panel with a search field, shared-library toggles, and grid/list layout controls before insertion.

references.title: Component details preview popover
references.question: Q1
references.take: Figma uses a focused details popup to inspect a reusable review-card component before committing it to the canvas.

references.title: Browse a filtered lesson library
references.question: Q1
references.take: Library shows search, category chips, Filters/Clear filters, and categorized lesson rows; it is learner discovery with no author add action.

references.title: Create and publish course
references.question: Q1
references.take: Shows an empty course list and a guided create-course wizard, not reusable-library browsing or scenario preview/add.

references.title: Choose and copy a design into a course
references.question: Q2
references.take: Choose design searches existing work, offers Copy to course or Move, and returns the copied item to Activities; only one design can be selected.

references.title: Add quiz questions one at a time
references.question: Q2
references.take: Add question configures and commits one original quiz question per modal; no library, multi-select, or batch add is visible.

references.title: Add items from a content library with selection and batch add
references.question: Q2
references.take: Searchable Content Library supports multiple selected cards, Deselect all, a count-aware Add 2 items action, and immediate insertion of both blocks.

references.title: Import selected lessons from another course
references.question: Q2
references.take: Import content selects a source course, exposes row/section checkboxes plus Select all/none, imports several lessons in one action, then shows them in Curriculum with a completion toast.

references.title: Build a quiz by adding questions within a lesson
references.question: Q2
references.take: Quiz builder edits one question and its answers inline, then offers New question; useful authoring counterexample, with no reusable-library batch selection.

references.title: Apply changes to a template instance
references.question: Q3
references.take: AI request, three generated choices, selected design, Color control, and Use Canva Editor handoff suggest choose-then-edit template-copy semantics; no source link, propagation, or overrides shown. Candidate counterexample.

references.title: Attach text to an existing library component
references.question: Q3
references.take: Select text → Library → Attach to existing component → select exact-match hero-title → Attach → linked label and confirmation toast. Propagation and overrides unverified.

references.title: Insert and configure a component instance
references.question: Q3
references.take: Browse library → Cards → Review Card details → Insert instance → choose variable mode → place card; selected instance visibly names Review Card and Simple Design System source. Propagation and override survival unverified.

references.title: Insert a synced block from the advanced blocks menu
references.question: Q3
references.take: Advanced blocks visibly offers Synced block as an insertion choice; created block, source identity, edits, propagation, and overrides are not shown.

references.title: Reorder lessons and sections in a course
references.question: Q4
references.take: Five frames show a newly present fifth lesson, the complete Culinary Explorations section lifted, moved above The World of Potatoes, and settled with lesson membership and Draft states preserved.

references.title: Course outline with modules, statuses, and add content
references.question: Q4
references.take: One authoring screen shows four grouped modules, Add Content controls, collapse controls, and Draft, Publish, Drip, and Lock labels; no ordering action or prerequisite setup is shown.

references.title: Course lessons grouped into sections with delayed release
references.question: Q4
references.take: The authoring screen shows New lesson and New section controls, lessons grouped in sections, and a module labeled Delayed 1 day; no reorder action or item prerequisite is shown.

references.title: Curriculum outline with draggable lessons and sections
references.question: Q4
references.take: A sectioned curriculum shows lesson rows and creation controls; an open Drip panel configures release by date or days after enrollment. Grip icons are visible, but movement is not demonstrated.

references.title: Curriculum grouped into numbered sections
references.question: Q4
references.take: The learner view shows 14 sections, 88 lectures, numbered lessons in an expanded first section, and collapsed later sections; authoring, reorder, and prerequisite controls are absent.

references.title: Course outline with numbered sections and activity duration
references.question: Q5
references.take: Desktop learner outline shows numbered sections and an expanded activity with sequence, thumbnail, title, description, and 5-minute duration.

references.title: Mobile curriculum with numbered sections and lesson duration
references.question: Q5
references.take: Mobile curriculum shows numbered sections and expanded activity cards with sequence, thumbnail, title, and a 4-minute estimate where supplied.

references.title: Program detail flow with lesson count, duration, enrollment, and lesson list
references.question: Q5
references.take: Program detail shows 29 lessons and 11h 34m; its Lessons view shows per-item minutes, and a resource card shows type plus 5-minute duration. Automatic source-to-outline copying is not shown.

references.title: AI-assisted course outline workspace
references.question: Q5
references.take: Outline creation asks for course title and student-facing description and offers AI generation, but no curriculum item metadata or transfer is visible.

references.title: Course lecture list with durations, section grouping, and downloads
references.question: Q5
references.take: Learner lecture outline keeps section, lesson number, media type, title, remaining duration, and download affordance together.

references.title: Empty lessons state with inline add controls
references.question: Q6
references.take: Shows 1 section, 0 lessons, editable Untitled section - 1, Add new, and Add section. No suggestions, examples, guidance, or library route.

references.title: Generated course outline with search and add content
references.question: Q6
references.take: Confirms successful outline creation, then shows search, three populated modules, global and module Add content actions, expandable rows, and Draft controls. Generation itself is not shown.

references.title: Search with an explicit no-results state
references.question: Q6
references.take: Reports No results found for “buddism” while category controls, filters, and an unrelated Terence Tao course card remain visible, creating an ambiguous empty-result state; counterexample.

references.title: Course builder with setup guidance and starter outline
references.question: Q6
references.take: Combines How to create an online course/See how guidance, New lesson/New section actions, and starter content with sample text, video, and quiz lessons.

references.title: Course creation onboarding from empty state
references.question: Q6
references.take: Empty Courses table explains where created courses appear and offers Create course plus Learn more. Only the flow entry screen is available locally, so later steps are unverified.

references.title: Choose a course outline method
references.question: Q6
references.take: Step 5/5 presents Generate with AI from a description, Start from scratch, and Bulk upload as distinct curriculum paths, with Back and Finish controls.
